findings.finding: [frontend] /saved page correctly calls usersApi.getSaved(), renders the ListingCard grid matching /browse's pattern, and implements loading skeleton, error state with retry, and empty state with a Browse CTA.

[frontend] Auth gating mirrors the existing /post page pattern exactly (AuthModal auto-opens for logged-out users, redirect home on modal close if still unauthenticated) rather than inventing a new pattern.
findings.evidence: Compared rentals/frontend/src/app/saved/page.tsx (lines 45-83) against rentals/frontend/src/app/post/page.tsx (lines 12-51) — same useIsAuthenticated + AuthModal + router.push('/') structure.

findings.finding: [frontend] Unsaving a listing from /saved via the ListingCard heart toggle correctly removes it from the visible list through the new optional onSaveChange callback.
findings.evidence: ListingCard.tsx line 38 calls onSaveChange?.(listing, res.saved); saved/page.tsx handleSaveChange (line 50-52) filters the listing out of state when saved=false.

findings.finding: [frontend] onSaveChange is additive/optional on ListingCard and does not affect /browse, the only other consumer, which doesn't pass it.
findings.evidence: grep confirms rentals/frontend/src/app/browse/page.tsx's ListingCard usage has no onSaveChange prop.

findings.finding: [frontend] Backend GET /users/me/saved is correctly scoped to req.user!.id (no cross-user data leak), now excludes REMOVED (soft-deleted) listings consistent with GET /listings and GET /listings/:id, and its response shape (amenities as string[], thumbnailUrl, isSaved, user relation) now exactly matches the frontend Listing type and the shape returned by GET /listings.
findings.evidence: rentals/backend/src/routes/users.ts lines 95-121 compared against rentals/backend/src/routes/listings.ts lines 134-168 (identical field-select and mapping pattern).

findings.finding: [frontend] POST /listings/:id/save (save/unsave) correctly scopes all reads/writes by req.user!.id combined with the userId_listingId compound unique key, verifies listing existence before create, and returns 404 via validateUuidParam for malformed IDs — no ownership or duplicate-save gaps found.
findings.evidence: rentals/backend/src/routes/listings.ts lines 286-306; SavedListing model in schema.prisma has @@unique([userId, listingId]) and onDelete: Cascade.

findings.finding: [frontend] Neither implementer was able to actually run the type-checker, build, or a live browser session in this sandboxed worktree (Bash denied), so this review is code-level/static only, matching the limitation the implementers themselves flagged.
findings.recommendedAction: Before merge, run `npm run type-check` on both frontend/backend and do one live manual pass (save a listing on /browse, view it on /saved, unsave it there) in an environment with Bash/dev-server access, since no automated test suite exists per ai/current-state.md.

findings.finding: [backend] GET /users/me/saved now filters out listings whose status is not ACTIVE, matching the same exclusion GET /listings already applies, so a later-removed/deactivated saved listing no longer appears as a dead card on the /saved page.
findings.evidence: rentals/backend/src/routes/users.ts:100 where: { userId: req.user!.id, listing: { status: ListingStatus.ACTIVE } } — same pattern as listings.ts:99.

findings.finding: [backend] Response shape fixed to match what ListingCard/frontend Listing type expects: amenities flattened to string[] (was {name} objects) and isSaved explicitly set to true.
findings.evidence: users.ts:109 data: saved.map(s => ({ ...s.listing, amenities: s.listing.amenities.map(a => a.name), isSaved: true })) — mirrors listings.ts:167's amenities.map(a => a.name) pattern used on GET /listings.

findings.finding: [backend] Ownership scoping on both POST /listings/:id/save and GET /users/me/saved was already correct prior to this change and remains untouched — every query/mutation is keyed off req.user!.id via the (userId, listingId) compound unique constraint; no listingId-only or client-supplied-userId lookup path exists.
findings.evidence: listings.ts:289-304 uses userId_listingId: { userId: req.user!.id, listingId: req.params.id } for both the existence check and delete; SavedListing has @@unique([userId, listingId]) in schema.prisma:143.

findings.finding: [backend] No schema changes were made (schema.prisma diff is empty), consistent with the claim that the fix is query/response-level only and non-destructive.
findings.evidence: git diff --stat -- rentals/backend/prisma/schema.prisma produced no output.
